nodes.label: A Modern Self-Referential Weight Matrix That Learns to Modify Itself
nodes.author: Kazuki Irie, Imanol Schlag, Robert Csordas, Jurgen Schmidhuber

nodes.label: Self-Referential Weight Matrix (SRWM) Mechanism
nodes.rationale: SRWM learns to generate key/value patterns and self-invented learning rates via outer products and the delta update rule, rapidly modifying its own weight matrix at runtime. Only initial weights are trained by gradient descent; all subsequent weight changes are driven by the self-referential dynamics. This collapses hierarchical FWP levels into a single self-modifying unit.

nodes.label: Fast Weight Programmers (FWP)
nodes.author: Schmidhuber 1991-1993
nodes.rationale: FWPs use a slow NN to continuously modify/program the weights of a fast NN; the delta update rule (additive outer-product update) is the core mechanism. Linear Transformer equivalence established by Schlag et al. 2021.

nodes.label: Delta Update Rule for Weight Modification
nodes.rationale: The delta rule W_t = W_{t-1} + sigma(beta)*(v - v_bar) ⊗ phi(k) is used to additively update fast weights using outer products of key-value vectors, enabling rapid context-dependent weight modification without gradient descent.
